name: FIELD_PREP_WM16
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression. It copies _val into a local __val and _mask into a local __mask (each argument is evaluated once), runs __BF_FIELD_CHECK(__mask, (u16)0U, __val, ...), which only contains compile-time build checks (mask constant and non-zero, mask contiguous, mask not wider than 16 bits, and, for a constant value, that the value fits in the field) and no runtime check, and then yields (((typeof(__mask))__val << __bf_shf(__mask)) & __mask) | (__mask << 16), where __bf_shf is the trailing-zero count of the mask. The result has the type of the mask: the value shifted into the field position and masked, ORed with the mask shifted up by 16 bits.
note: Macro; no contract (unbound __bf_shf in the earlier attempt). Checked __BF_FIELD_CHECK in include/linux/bitfield.h.

name: FIELD_PREP_WM16_CONST
prose: Function-like macro that is a constant expression. It evaluates to FIELD_PREP_CONST(_mask, _val) | (BUILD_BUG_ON_ZERO(const_true((u64)(_mask) > U16_MAX)) + ((_mask) << 16)). FIELD_PREP_CONST yields the value shifted into the mask position and masked, with its own compile-time checks (non-zero mask, contiguous mask, value fits). The second part is a compile-time error if the mask is larger than U16_MAX and otherwise contributes the mask shifted up by 16 bits. There is no runtime check; _mask and _val are expanded more than once.
note: Macro; no contract (unbound FIELD_PREP_CONST in the earlier attempt).

name: proto_ports_offset
prose: Returns a byte offset by switch on proto: 0 for IPPROTO_TCP, IPPROTO_UDP, IPPROTO_DCCP, IPPROTO_ESP, IPPROTO_SCTP and IPPROTO_UDPLITE; 4 for IPPROTO_AH; and -EINVAL for any other value. It reads nothing but its argument and changes no state.
note: Three-way switch with exactly these returns (scratch-dump lines 101-113). Contract left empty: the earlier attempts were rejected only because errno names in the prose are not in the contract.

name: ITSTATIC void ITPREFIX ## _insert(ITSTRUCT *node, struct rb_root_cached *root)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_insert for ITPREFIX = interval_tree). Walks down from root->rb_root.rb_node. At each visited node it raises that node's ITSUBTREE to last = ITLAST(node) if it is smaller, then goes left if ITSTART(node) < ITSTART(visited) and otherwise goes right (clearing the leftmost flag; equal starts go right). It sets node->ITSUBTREE = last, links the node at the found position with rb_link_node, and calls rb_insert_augmented_cached(&node->ITRB, root, leftmost, &ITPREFIX_augment), which rebalances and updates the cached leftmost pointer. Returns nothing. node must not already be in a tree. It takes no lock; callers must serialise access to the tree.
note: Unreviewed before (mechanical name-only rejections); rewritten from the macro body. Named by the generated definition head.

name: ITSTATIC void ITPREFIX ## _remove(ITSTRUCT *node, struct rb_root_cached *root)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_remove). It is a single call rb_erase_augmented_cached(&node->ITRB, root, &ITPREFIX_augment), which unlinks the node from the cached augmented rbtree, rebalances, and runs the augment callbacks to recompute the ITSUBTREE maxima and updates the cached leftmost pointer. Returns nothing. node must be in the tree rooted at root; no lock is taken here.
note: Named by the generated definition head. Behaviour of the augmented erase itself is in the rbtree code, not re-derived here.

name: static ITSTRUCT * ITPREFIX ## _subtree_search(ITSTRUCT *node, ITTYPE start, ITTYPE last)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_subtree_search); static, not governed by ITSTATIC. Loops with node as the current subtree root. If node has a left child and start <= left->ITSUBTREE it moves to the left child. Otherwise, if ITSTART(node) <= last: if start <= ITLAST(node) it returns node, else it moves to node's right child (taken without a NULL check, relying on the loop invariant start <= node->ITSUBTREE). If ITSTART(node) > last it returns NULL. So for a subtree satisfying the invariant it returns the leftmost node whose interval intersects [start, last], or NULL. It reads the tree and changes nothing.
note: Named by the generated definition head. The right-child step has no NULL test; correctness depends on the caller establishing start <= node->ITSUBTREE (iter_first checks it, iter_next checks start <= right->ITSUBTREE).

name: ITSTATIC ITSTRUCT * ITPREFIX ## _iter_first(struct rb_root_cached *root, ITTYPE start, ITTYPE last)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_iter_first). Returns NULL if the tree is empty (root->rb_root.rb_node is NULL), or if the root node's ITSUBTREE is less than start, or if ITSTART of root->rb_leftmost is greater than last. Otherwise it returns ITPREFIX_subtree_search(root node, start, last), i.e. the leftmost node whose interval intersects [start, last], or NULL if none does. It only reads the tree.
note: Named by the generated definition head. All three early NULL returns checked against scratch-dump lines 312-334.

name: ITSTATIC ITSTRUCT * ITPREFIX ## _iter_next(ITSTRUCT *node, ITTYPE start, ITTYPE last)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_iter_next). Given a node already known to satisfy ITSTART(node) <= last, it looks for the next intersecting node in start order. Loop: if node has a right child whose ITSUBTREE >= start it returns ITPREFIX_subtree_search on that child (which may itself return NULL). Otherwise it climbs through rb_parent until it arrives from a left child, returning NULL if it reaches the root. At that ancestor it returns NULL if last < ITSTART(ancestor), returns the ancestor if start <= ITLAST(ancestor), and otherwise repeats from the ancestor. Only reads the tree.
note: Named by the generated definition head. Returns checked against scratch-dump lines 342-374.

name: ipmi_demangle_device_id
prose: Parses an IPMI Get Device ID response in data (data_len bytes) into *id. Returns -EINVAL, leaving *id untouched, if data_len < 7, or if netfn is not IPMI_NETFN_APP_RESPONSE or cmd is not IPMI_GET_DEVICE_ID_CMD, or if data[0] (the completion code) is nonzero. Otherwise it skips the first byte and sets device_id, device_revision, firmware_revision_1, firmware_revision_2, ipmi_version and additional_device_support from original bytes 1 to 6. If at least 12 bytes were given it sets manufacturer_id (original bytes 7 to 9, little endian) and product_id (bytes 10 and 11), otherwise both are set to 0. If at least 16 bytes were given it copies original bytes 12 to 15 into aux_firmware_revision and sets aux_firmware_revision_set to 1, otherwise it sets that flag to 0 (aux_firmware_revision is not written). Then returns 0. It takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the real name is ipmi_demangle_device_id (include/linux/ipmi_smi.h). The earlier prose said it always returns 0; wrong, there are three -EINVAL returns before the parsing.

name: __gicv3_prio_to_ns
prose: Function-like macro: expands to (0xff & ((p) << 1)), i.e. p shifted left by one and truncated to the low 8 bits, so bit 7 of p is discarded.
note: Macro; no contract. Old prose said 'the low byte of p shifted left', which reverses the order of mask and shift.

name: __gicv3_ns_to_prio
prose: Function-like macro: expands to (0x80 | ((ns) >> 1)): ns shifted right by one with bit 7 set. For ns in 0..255 this is a value from 0x80 to 0xff.
note: Macro; no contract.

name: rpmi_to_linux_error
prose: Maps an RPMI error code to a Linux errno by switch. Returns 0 for RPMI_SUCCESS (0); -EINVAL for RPMI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM (-3), RPMI_ERR_BAD_RANGE (-11) and RPMI_ERR_INVALID_STATE (-10); -EPERM for RPMI_ERR_DENIED (-4); -EFAULT for RPMI_ERR_INVALID_ADDR (-5) and RPMI_ERR_HW_FAULT (-8); -EALREADY for RPMI_ERR_ALREADY (-6); -EBUSY for RPMI_ERR_BUSY (-9); -ETIMEDOUT for RPMI_ERR_TIMEOUT (-12); -ECOMM for RPMI_ERR_IO (-13); and -EOPNOTSUPP for RPMI_ERR_FAILED (-1), RPMI_ERR_NOTSUPP (-2), RPMI_ERR_NO_DATA (-14), RPMI_ERR_EXTENSION (-7) and every other value (default). It changes no state.
note: Checked each case against scratch-dump lines 606-631. Contract left empty because the earlier ones were rejected for not naming the errno macros used in the prose.

name: nf_hook
prose: Inline entry point that runs the registered netfilter hooks for (pf, hook). It returns 1 when the caller should continue by calling okfn itself; any other value means the packet was consumed. Steps: (1) with CONFIG_JUMP_LABEL, if pf and hook are compile-time constants and static_key_false(&nf_hooks_needed[pf][hook]) is false, it returns 1 at once. (2) It takes rcu_read_lock and picks hook_head by pf: net->nf.hooks_ipv4[hook] for NFPROTO_IPV4, hooks_ipv6[hook] for NFPROTO_IPV6, hooks_arp[hook] for NFPROTO_ARP (only with CONFIG_NETFILTER_FAMILY_ARP, and with WARN_ON_ONCE and no hook list if hook is out of range), hooks_bridge[hook] for NFPROTO_BRIDGE (only with CONFIG_NETFILTER_FAMILY_BRIDGE), and WARN_ON_ONCE with no hook list for any other pf; the IPv4, IPv6 and bridge indexes are not range checked here. (3) If a hook list was found it fills a struct nf_hook_state with nf_hook_state_init(hook, pf, indev, outdev, sk, net, okfn) and sets ret = nf_hook_slow(skb, &state, hook_head, 0). (4) It releases the RCU read lock and returns ret, which is still 1 if there was no hook list. nf_hook_slow returns 1 when every hook accepted; a negative errno when a hook returned NF_DROP (skb freed, -EPERM if the verdict encodes no errno); NF_DROP_GETERR(verdict), 0 or a negative errno encoded by the hook, for NF_STOLEN; nf_queue's result for NF_QUEUE (1 if queueing failed with -ESRCH and the verdict carries the queue-bypass flag, in which case processing continues with the next hook; otherwise 0, whether the packet was queued or queueing failed and nf_queue freed the skb); and 0 after a WARN_ON_ONCE for an unknown verdict, leaving the skb to the caller. nf_hook itself never calls okfn.
note: Reviewers mixed: round 1 right (return is nf_hook_slow's errno/0/1 rather than a raw verdict); round 2 wrong direction (an unknown verdict returns 0, not 1 or a negative errno); round 15 right that unknown verdict returns 0 but wrong that nf_hook_slow does not WARN (net/netfilter/core.c nf_hook_slow default: WARN_ON_ONCE(1); return 0;). The old prose said an unknown verdict gives 1: corrected. Slice cut the tail: rest of nf_hook read from include/linux/netfilter.h.

name: __ONCE_LITE_IF
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression with a function-local static bool __already_done (placed in section .data..once) separate for each place where the macro is expanded. It evaluates condition once into __ret_cond; if __ret_cond is true and __already_done is false it sets __already_done to true and the macro yields true, otherwise it yields false (without touching the flag when the condition is false). The test and the set are plain, not atomic, so concurrent callers may both see the flag clear. The yield is wrapped in unlikely().
note: Reviewer right that the old contract omitted the flag being set; contract dropped. Old prose said 'permanently' and did not mention the non-atomic test-and-set.

name: DO_ONCE_LITE_IF
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression. It evaluates condition once into __ret_do_once (as !!condition); if __ONCE_LITE_IF(__ret_do_once) is true it calls func(__VA_ARGS__). The macro yields unlikely(__ret_do_once), the truth value of the condition, whether or not func was called. Because the guard is a per-expansion-site static flag tested and set without atomics, func is called at most once per expansion site only when callers do not race; concurrent first callers may each call it. DO_ONCE_LITE(func, ...) is the same with condition true.
note: Reviewer right: the old claim that func runs at most once across all calls was too strong (per expansion site, and not atomic). Contract dropped.

name: adjust_by_scaled_ppm
prose: Returns base adjusted by scaled_ppm parts per million with a 16-bit binary fraction. It calls diff_by_scaled_ppm(base, scaled_ppm, &diff): if scaled_ppm is negative it negates it (undefined behaviour for the most negative long), and diff = mul_u64_u64_div_u64(base, (u64)|scaled_ppm|, 1000000ULL << 16), which in the generic implementation uses a 128-bit intermediate and returns U64_MAX when the quotient does not fit in 64 bits (an architecture may supply its own version). If scaled_ppm was negative the result is base - diff, otherwise base + diff, both in u64 arithmetic, so the result wraps modulo 2^64 if diff exceeds base or the sum overflows. No locks or memory are involved.
note: Reviewers right about the contract (hardcoded LONG_MIN / INT_MIN exclusions, and the underflow requirement); contract removed rather than patched. Prose now says what the u64 arithmetic does instead of excluding overflow inputs. mul_u64_u64_div_u64 read in lib/math/div64.c.

name: raid_set_##attr(struct raid_template *r, struct device *dev, type value)
prose: Generated by DEFINE_RAID_ATTRIBUTE(enum raid_level, level) as raid_set_level(r, dev, value). It looks up the class device for dev with attribute_container_find_class_device(&r->raid_attrs.ac, dev), and executes BUG_ON(!device), a kernel BUG if none is found. Otherwise it takes rd = dev_get_drvdata(device) and stores value into rd->level, with no range check, returning nothing. It assumes the drvdata of that class device is a struct raid_data. It takes no lock itself.
note: Unreviewed before; checked against the macro body and attribute_container_find_class_device (drivers/base/attribute_container.c), which returns NULL when no class device has dev as parent. Named by the generated definition head.

name: DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1(srcu, struct srcu_struct, _T->idx = srcu_read_lock(_T->lock), srcu_read_unlock(_T->lock, _T->idx), int idx)
prose: Macro invocation (DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1 in cleanup.h) that generates the guard type class_srcu_t, a struct holding struct srcu_struct *lock and int idx, plus class_srcu_destructor and class_srcu_constructor, class_srcu_lock_ptr and class_srcu_lock_err. class_srcu_constructor(l) stores l in .lock, runs idx = srcu_read_lock(lock), and returns the guard by value. class_srcu_destructor calls srcu_read_unlock(lock, idx) unless the stored lock pointer is NULL or an error pointer (__GUARD_IS_ERR). Used through guard(srcu)(...) or scoped_guard(srcu, ...), the unlock runs when the guard variable leaves scope.

name: __svc_print_addr
prose: Formats a socket address into buf with snprintf(buf, len, ...) and returns buf. For sa_family AF_INET it prints "%pI4, port=%u" with the IPv4 address and ntohs of the port; for AF_INET6 it prints "%pI6, port=%u" with the IPv6 address and port; for any other family it prints "unknown address type: %d" with the family number. snprintf writes at most len bytes including the terminating NUL, truncating longer output, and nothing if len is 0. The address is cast to struct sockaddr_in or sockaddr_in6 only in the matching case. The function returns buf in all cases and does not check that buf is non-NULL.
note: slice cut the head: the real name is __svc_print_addr (verified in include/linux/sunrpc/svc_xprt.h); the old name format_addr does not exist in the file.

name: ssh_tid_is_valid
prose: Returns ssh_tid_to_index(tid) < SSH_NUM_TARGETS. ssh_tid_to_index returns the u8 value tid - 1u (so tid 0 gives 255) and SSH_NUM_TARGETS is 2, so the function returns true exactly when tid is 1 or 2 and false for every other u8 value including 0. It has no side effects.
note: Old prose said it returns true for every tid and that ssh_tid_to_index returns -EINVAL: both wrong (include/linux/surface_aggregator/serial_hub.h: ssh_tid_to_index is `return tid - 1u;` with u8 return, SSH_NUM_TARGETS is 2). The round 1 reviewer claim (invalid tids map to -EINVAL and give true) is also wrong for the same reason.

name: static ssize_t __struct##_##__name##_store(struct config_item *item, const char *page, size_t len)
prose: Generated by GS_STRINGS_W(__struct, __name); the generated function is named <struct>_<name>_store. It takes gs = to_<struct>(item) and calls usb_string_copy(page, &gs-><name>). If that returns nonzero the store returns that value; otherwise it returns len. usb_string_copy (drivers/usb/gadget/configfs.c) returns -EOVERFLOW if strlen(page) exceeds USB_MAX_STRING_LEN, -EINVAL if page is empty, and -ENOMEM if it needs a new buffer and kmalloc fails; on any of these the field pointer is unchanged and nothing is freed. On success it copies page into the existing buffer of the field if there is one, otherwise into a newly kmalloc'ed buffer of USB_MAX_STRING_WITH_NULL_LEN bytes, strips one trailing newline, and sets the field to that buffer. len is used only as the return value.
note: Reviewer wrong: usb_string_copy never frees the old field (lib code at drivers/usb/gadget/configfs.c:113-135 has no kfree), so the field is unchanged on -ENOMEM. The old prose missed the -EINVAL path for an empty string; added.

When CONFIG_OF is enabled the header only declares of_usb_update_otg_caps and the real function is defined elsewhere (it returns -EINVAL for a NULL otg_caps or an unsupported otg-rev and otherwise updates *otg_caps), so the always-0 result describes only the stub.

name: find_closest
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression yielding an index of type typeof(as). With __fc_as = as - 1, it scans i from 0 while i < as - 1: mid = (a[i] + a[i+1]) / 2 (integer division, in the element type); at the first i with x <= mid it computes left = x - a[i] and right = a[i+1] - x, increments i if right < left (so a tie keeps the lower index), and stops. If no such i is found the loop ends with i = as - 1. The array a is expected to be sorted ascending; x, a and as are each evaluated once, and x is converted to long.
